llmResponse.agendaChanges: No formal changes to the agenda were proposed or adopted. Section 7 (Bond Program Action Items) and Section 10 (Discussion Items) had no items taken up. The Approval of Consent Items (Section 11) was handled as a bundle after the school presentations. Section 9 Action Items (SPSA approvals) were each voted on immediately after the corresponding school presentation rather than as a separate block.

publicComments.name: Kristi Herrera
publicComments.summary: Kindergarten teacher at Hoover with 24 years of experience described challenges of large class sizes and high proportions of students with IEPs, multilingual learners, and behavioral needs, urging the board to create classrooms structured for learning.

publicComments.name: Sandy Hoover
publicComments.summary: Retired Redwood City kindergarten teacher advocated for smaller class sizes and faster timelines for identifying and assessing students with special needs.

publicComments.name: Erin Washburn
publicComments.summary: Music teacher and RCTA Membership Chair announced that the Redwood City Teachers Association unanimously voted to endorse the Redwood City School District parcel tax.

publicComments.name: Thomas Rogerson
publicComments.summary: Parent of children at Henry Ford and North Star argued that teacher quality matters most to student achievement, urged the board to consider equity and teacher retention when evaluating class sizes, and noted that heterogeneous classrooms deserve more targeted support.

publicComments.name: Aracely Flores Mendoza
publicComments.summary: Second-year education specialist at Hoover described unsustainable caseloads for resource teachers and requested that the board provide two aides for resource teachers at Hoover for the next school year.

publicComments.name: Ann Briljafa
publicComments.summary: Retired teacher shared data about TK students' IEPs, SSTs, and behavioral challenges arriving in next year's kindergarten, arguing that small class sizes in kindergarten are essential to early literacy outcomes.

publicComments.name: Lisbeth Estrada and Jesus Ponce
publicComments.summary: Hoover parents (speaking in Spanish with English translation) thanked the district for investments at Hoover and requested extended TK hours, expansion of TK, and instructional assistants in kindergarten and first grade to support personalized learning.

publicComments.name: Heather McCormick
publicComments.summary: Henry Ford parent and classroom volunteer described how a class of 32 third graders limits space for curriculum activities and leaves some students without adequate attention.

publicComments.name: Augustine Espino
publicComments.summary: Parent and community advocate expressed concern about large class sizes, reported that he has been spreading awareness of the parcel tax among parents, and urged accountability to the Latino community if the tax passes.

publicComments.name: Pam Barash
publicComments.summary: 36-year kindergarten teacher at Henry Ford described how student needs have grown dramatically over her career and urged the board not to allow kindergarten class sizes to reach 30-to-1, warning that joyful personalized learning is impossible at that ratio.

publicComments.name: Lilia Amalia Valdez-Monet
publicComments.summary: Hoover parent since 2017 described firsthand observations of the impact of having only one Spanish kindergarten class and asked the board to reduce class sizes and restore a second Spanish kindergarten section.

publicComments.name: Patricia Renderos
publicComments.summary: Parent (speaking in Spanish) expressed excitement about TK results, said she is encouraging other families to enroll in TK, and thanked the board and teachers for their work.

publicComments.name: Sophia Santos
publicComments.summary: First-grade teacher at Hoover in her first year with the district shared that managing 27 students with varied needs is overwhelming and urged the board to take steps to reduce class sizes.

publicComments.name: Jackie Moore
publicComments.summary: Special education teacher and Hoover parent advocated for paraeducators in every K-2 classroom, smaller class sizes, a hard cap on SLC caseloads, and a para for each RLC teacher.

publicComments.name: Rajanesh Patarath
publicComments.summary: Marine Corps veteran and father of a kindergarten student in Ms. Herrera's class praised her teaching and asked the board to consider the impact of increasing class sizes on students' ability to receive individualized attention.

publicComments.name: Brenna Gear
publicComments.summary: RCTA President asked the board to officially endorse the Prop 55 extension and announced that over upcoming board meetings teachers will speak on negotiation topics including class size, salary, and safety.

publicComments.name: Unidentified speaker (CSEA/classified representative)
publicComments.summary: Classified employees' representative argued that classified staff consistently receive less equitable compensation than teachers and administrators and called on the board to provide fair and equitable salary increases that reflect the real cost of living.
